transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Head of ML, Luminex), Marcus Bell (Eng Mgr, Luminex), Sara Chen (Security Lead, Luminex)

Auto-summary: quick review of last run's scorecard, a couple of false positive guardrail hits, discussion of prompt drift on two templates, request for regression traces on quantized profile, agreement to share guardrail playbook and run larger regression sweep.

Topics covered: Scorecard anomalies, prompt set triage, guardrail tuning, dedicated vs hosted latency considerations, security docs request.

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Ethan: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check, can you all hear me?
[00:02] Priya: Yeah loud and clear, Ethan.
[00:04] Marcus: Yep, same here.
[00:10] Ethan: Great. So agenda for today, we wanted to walk through the scorecard from last night's run, highlight the regressions, and then go into guardrail tuning. Maya and I will share screens after the high-level. Sound good?
[00:18] Priya: Sounds good. We're particularly interested in the flagged templates — the customer-facing FAQ and the claims summarizer — those had some user-facing noise.
[00:26] Maya: Cool. I'll try to keep the deep-dive concrete, but quick note — some of the transcription in the exported logs looks weird, like KV cash instead of KV cache, so apologies if anything reads odd.
[00:36] Sara: That's fine. Also, can we make sure the security asks are near the top? We need the SOC2 reviewer contact.
[00:40] Ethan: Absolutely, we'll cover that in the last 10 minutes.

[00:45] Ethan: All right, slide 2 — overall pass rate held at 92% which is stable, but earn attention on two buckets: hallucination-type failures in claims summarizer and guardrail false positives on the FAQ template.
[00:58] Marcus: When you say hallucination failures — is that content inventing policy numbers or just adding extra steps?
[01:04] Maya: Mostly insertion of extraneous details, like invented policy dates and references. In our scoring, that pushes to a critical fail.
[01:10] Priya: Right, we start to see users complain when it invents a policy that doesn't exist.

[01:18] Ethan: So first anomaly — claims summarizer, we saw a 6% regression on the hallucination score after we switched to the quantized 8-bit profile for the weekend run.
[01:28] Priya: Wait, that's the quantized model? We thought quantization was safe for summarization workloads.
[01:33] Maya: It usually is but there are edge cases — long context with lots of numeric tokens seems to exacerbate tokenization artifacts. We suspect the int8 kernels slightly degrade numerical fidelity.
[01:42] Marcus: Hmm, that matches an internal note — when we compressed numeric-heavy documents we saw token boundaries shift.
[01:48] Sara: From a compliance angle, any change that creates hallucinations is a red flag. Can we pin to hosted full-precision for the customer-facing endpoint until we validate?
[01:56] Ethan: Yes, that's one proposed mitigation — pin the production route to full-precision hosted model and use quantized for batch/background tasks.
[02:04] Priya: That would work, but it impacts cost. How big is the unit cost delta?
[02:09] Ethan: For this workload, full-precision hosted is roughly 2.8x token cost versus the quantized dedicated profile. But latency improves slightly on dedicated with batching — tradeoffs.
[02:18] Marcus: We need a number we can show execs. Can you include the per-100k token delta in the follow-up spreadsheet?
[02:24] Ethan: Yep, will do.

[02:30] Maya: Moving on to the FAQ false positives — the guardrail is catching polite language and tagging it as PII in about 1.2% of cases; it's mostly formatted addresses and phone numbers embedded in example snippets.
[02:42] Priya: Are these actual customer data or example placeholders?
[02:45] Marcus: I think placeholders, like 555-1212 or 123 Main St, but the guardrail logic treats numbers with dashes as potential PII.
[02:52] Maya: Exactly. The regex is a bit aggressive — it flags any dash-separated numeric token. We can relax the regex or apply context-aware heuristics.
[02:59] Sara: Relaxing regex worries me — we don't want to miss real PII. Could we instead add a post-classifier that checks semantic context before flagging?
[03:07] Maya: Yeah that's an option — add a small binary classifier that checks contextual cues, and only escalate when both regex and classifier agree. It adds a tiny latency, maybe 15–25ms per request.
[03:17] Priya: Latency budget is tight for our interactive FAQ — target p95 is < 300ms. Are we still within that if we add classifier?
[03:24] Ethan: With current routing and 2x autoscale it's borderline but still under 300ms; the extra classifier at 15–25ms bumps us but still under 320ms p95 — we'd need to either accept a slightly higher SLO or change routing (e.g., use dedicated capacity in region).
[03:36] Marcus: Could we do classifier in async for low-risk queries? But the user-facing needs immediate results.
[03:42] Maya: If it's interactive, async won't work. Another approach: run classifier only on cases where regex triggers — that keeps the classifier at ~1.2% of requests, so amortized latency impact is negligible.
[03:52] Sara: That sounds reasonable — only pay compute on suspected flags.
[03:55] Priya: Ok, let's do the conditional classifier. Please include false-positive reduction estimates in the playbook.

[04:02] Ethan: Quick note on scoring — we updated the threshold for hallucination score from 0.7 to 0.65 to be slightly stricter; that change is why you see some uptick in failures. We can rollback or calibrate with more samples.
[04:13] Priya: Hmm, can we see both curves? The pass rate with old threshold vs new threshold over the last four runs?
[04:19] Ethan: Yes, I'll attach the chart. Maya, can you show the sample bisection run?

[04:24] Maya: Yeah, I'm pulling up the bisection output — give me a second.
[04:32] [screen sharing noise]
[04:35] Maya: Alright, here's a set where we compared baseline FP16 run vs int8 quantized. You can see the regression concentrated on documents with long numeric tables — shot noise around row boundaries.
[04:47] Marcus: That makes sense. So practically, we should: 1) rollback the strict threshold, 2) pin customer-facing to FP16 hosted, 3) run a 2k-sample regression on quantized model to find edge cases.
[04:59] Ethan: That matches our recommendation. Any objections?
[05:03] Priya: No objections. We just need cost numbers and a timeline.
[05:08] Ethan: We'll send cost delta and the 2k regression plan by Friday.

[05:12] Sara: On security docs — can someone point me to where Redwood keeps the SOC2 artifact bundle? We need the SOC2 auditor contact for our procurement kickoff.
[05:20] Ethan: Sure, I'll share the Secure Docs link in the follow-up email. Maya, can you drop the contact?
[05:25] Maya: Yes, it's laura.holt@redwood-inference.com, and I'll include the SOC2 summary and the audit report link.
[05:31] Sara: Great, please include any KMS/HSM notes; we run KMS in-house.
[05:36] Maya: We'll include KMS integration notes and the options for customer-managed keys on Private deployments.

[05:42] Marcus: One more question about routing — if we pin to hosted full precision, do we lose the dedicated autoscale benefits?
[05:48] Ethan: Not necessarily — hosted full-precision is served from multi-tenant pools; you lose single-tenant autoscale guarantees. If you want guaranteed throughput and predictable p95, Redwood Dedicated can be configured with FP16 kernels, but that requires a reserved commit.
[06:01] Priya: That might be a sell for us if the quantized profile stays risky. We have to balance cost vs SLA.
[06:06] Ethan: Understood. We'll put a comparison table in the follow-up: Hosted FP16 vs Dedicated FP16 vs Dedicated Int8 quantized (expected perf, cost, and SLO notes).

[06:15] Maya: Back to the guardrail false positives — I ran a quick patch where we narrow the dash regex and add a contextual classifier; in 200-sample test it reduced false positives from 1.2% to 0.15% with no measurable increase in false negatives.
[06:29] Priya: Good. Do you have examples?
[06:31] Maya: Yes, I'll paste a few in the deck — one where "123-45-6789" was a real SSN that flagged, and one where "555-1212" was an example which the classifier suppressed.
[06:40] Marcus: Can we get the classifier model size and latency per call? Need to evaluate memory footprint for dedicated pools.
[06:46] Maya: It's a tiny transformer, ~20MB, latency ~12ms on the inference nodes; path only triggered on regex hit so minimal overhead.
[06:53] Sara: That aligns with our preferences. Please include CPU/memory numbers for our infra team.

[06:58] Ethan: Any other blockers? Priya?
[07:01] Priya: Not blockers but can you also include a link to the prompt set versioning? We want to understand how prompts changed between runs.
[07:07] Maya: Yes, prompts are versioned in the prompt registry — I'll include diffs for the two affected templates. Looks like we removed an explicit numeric-anchor line in v4 which might explain tokenization differences.
[07:17] Marcus: That could explain the boundary shift. Can we revert that change for claims summarizer and re-run?
[07:22] Priya: Let's not revert yet — run the regression first so we can show risk to leadership.
[07:26] Ethan: Good call. We'll run regression on the current prompt set and on the reverted prompt to compare.

[07:32] [15:32] Ethan: Quick logistics — Maya will run the 2k-sample regression using quantized profile and upload traces; I'll prepare cost delta and model deployment comparison; Priya will share SOC2 procurement contact.
[07:45] Priya: I'll share the contact by Monday, likely their name is Daniel Keene.
[07:49] Marcus: Also can you add a column in the spreadsheet for "user impact severity" so we can prioritize fixes?
[07:54] Ethan: Yep, we'll add that to the scoring CSV.

[08:00] Sara: One small transcription artifact — the export labeled a speaker as "Speaker 4" in a few places, might be Maya, but not critical.
[08:05] Maya: That's the automatic tool, yeah, sometimes flips names.

[08:08] Ethan: Okay last thing — recap of next steps verbally so it's crystal.
[08:12] Ethan: Action 1: Ethan to send guardrail playbook + scoring CSV + cost delta for FP16 vs Int8 by 2026-05-08.
[08:21] Ethan: Action 2: Maya to run 2,000-sample regression on quantized profile, upload traces and bisection results by 2026-05-14.
[08:29] Ethan: Action 3: Priya to confirm SOC2 procurement contact and share required security contacts by 2026-05-10.
[08:35] Ethan: Action 4: Maya to include prompt diff and example failure cases in the deck.
[08:40] Priya: Sounds good.
[08:42] Marcus: Thanks everyone.
[08:44] Sara: Thanks, bye.
[08:45] Ethan: Bye.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcription: there are occasional mis-hears (e.g., "KV cash" -> KV cache), speaker mislabeling, and timing markers approximate. Links referenced: guardrail playbook (link sent after meeting), scoring CSV (attached), SOC2 docs (secure link).
